text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your palms and tell me if it has been present since you were a child? Also, are you experiencing any weakness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your occupational history with rice farming and livestock, I suspect parasitic infection. REQUEST TEST: Skin Scraping_Acari

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any dark spots or linear tracks on your skin, particularly in the web spaces of your fingers? Also, does the itching worsen at night?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of hypopigmented macules, eyebrow thinning, and eyelash loss strongly suggests Hansen's disease (leprosy). REQUEST TEST: Slit-Skin_Smear_Acid_Fast_Bacilli

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the negative smear, the combination of hypopigmented macules, sensory loss, and adnexal changes like eyebrow thinning is highly suggestive of tuberculoid leprosy, which often has few bacilli. To confirm the diagnosis and assess nerve involvement, I need to evaluate the nerve function and skin histology. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study, Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Nerve_Conduction_Studies: Reduced sensory nerve action potentials in the ulnar nerves; Skin_Biopsy: Chronic inflammatory cells with features suggestive of leprosy

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical signs of hypopigmented macules, sensory loss, and adnexal changes, combined with nerve conduction deficits and suggestive biopsy results, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculoid Leprosy
